p.src: Now the Great Sage, accompanied by his two junior brothers, rode wind and cloud northeastward. In a moment they reached the entrance to Xuanying Cave on Azure Dragon Mountain. They descended from the clouds, and Bajie was about to smash down the gate. Wukong said, “Hold a moment. Let me go inside and see whether Master is alive or dead; then we can settle matters with them.” Sha Wujing said, “The gate is tightly shut. How can you get in?” Wukong replied, “I have powers of my own.”

p.src: Hearing these words, Wukong was overjoyed. Spreading his wings, he flew close to his master. Wiping away his tears, Tripitaka said, “Ah! Things are different here in the Western Regions. It is only the first month, when hibernating insects are just beginning to stir, so why is a firefly already abroad?” Unable to contain himself, Wukong called, “Master, I am here!” Tripitaka said delightedly, “Wukong! I was wondering how there could be a firefly in the first month. So it was you.” Wukong immediately resumed his true form and said, “Master, because you could not distinguish truth from falsehood, how much of our journey has been delayed and how much effort has been wasted! The moment I said they were no good, you bowed to them instead. Those fiends then dimmed the lamps, stole the aromatic oil blended with storax, and carried you off as well. I told Bajie and Sha Wujing to return and guard the monastery, while I followed the trail here, though I did not know the name of the place. Fortunately, I met the Four Duty Gods, who told me that this place was Xuanying Cave on Azure Dragon Mountain. I fought these fiends throughout the day and did not return until nightfall. After telling my junior brothers the whole affair, I did not sleep but came straight here with the two of them. I feared it would be inconvenient to fight so late at night, and I did not know what had become of you, so I transformed myself and came in to investigate.” Tripitaka asked happily, “Are Bajie and Sha Wujing outside now?” Wukong replied, “They are outside. When I looked just now, all the fiends were asleep. Let me undo the lock and force open the doors, then I will take you out.” Tripitaka nodded and thanked him.

p.src: Wukong used a lock-opening spell and merely brushed the lock with his hand; it sprang open at once. He was leading his master forward when suddenly a demon king called from a room off the central hall, “You underlings, keep the gates tightly shut and mind the lamps and fires! Why is no one calling the watches and making the rounds? Even the clappers and bells have fallen silent.” The lesser demons, exhausted by a full day of battle, had all fallen fast asleep. Hearing the call, they finally woke. As clappers and bells began to sound, several of them came from the rear, beating a gong and carrying weapons, and happened to run straight into master and disciple. The lesser demons all shouted, “You wretched monk! Where do you think you are going after wrenching open the lock?” Without pausing to argue, Wukong pulled out his cudgel and gave it a shake, making it as thick as a rice bowl, then struck. As the cudgel rose and fell, two demons were killed. The rest threw down their weapons, rushed to the central hall, and pounded on the door, crying, “Your Majesties, disaster! Disaster! The hairy-faced monk is killing people inside our own home!” Hearing this, the three fiends tumbled out of bed and cried only, “Seize him! Seize him!” Tripitaka was so terrified that his hands and feet went limp. Wukong could no longer attend to his master. Swinging his cudgel all the way, he fought his way forward. The lesser demons could not withstand him. He knocked down several and sent another two or three sprawling. He smashed through several gates, charged straight outside, and called, “Brothers, where are you?” Bajie and Sha Wujing were waiting with rake and staff raised. They asked, “Elder Brother, how did it go?” Wukong then related how he had transformed himself, gone inside, and freed their master, only for the demons to be alerted while they were leaving, forcing him to abandon their master and fight his way out. Of this no more need be said.

p.src: The demon kings seized Tripitaka and chained him up with the iron fetters once more. Holding swords and brandishing axes, with every lamp now blazing, they demanded, “How did you open the lock, you scoundrel? And how did that monkey get inside? Confess at once and we will spare your life; otherwise, we will cut you in two with a single stroke.” Terrified, Tripitaka fell trembling to his knees and said, “Most honored Kings, my disciple Sun Wukong knows seventy-two transformations. Just now he changed into a firefly and flew inside to rescue me. Unexpectedly, Your Majesties became aware of him, and he ran into your lesser captains. That witless disciple of mine injured two of them. Then everyone raised an alarm, took up arms, and lit the lamps, so he could no longer look after me and fled outside.” The three demon kings laughed aloud. “Fortunately we were alerted before he could get away with you.” They ordered their underlings to close the front and rear gates securely and make no noise.

p.src: Sha Wujing said, “They have shut the gates and fallen silent. I suspect they are secretly harming our master. Let us strike.” Wukong said, “You are right. Smash down the gate at once.” The simpleton showed off his divine strength, raised his rake, and brought it down with all his might, smashing the stone gate to pieces. Then he roared abuse, “You thieving oil-stealing fiends! Send our master out at once!” The lesser demons inside were so frightened that they tumbled back to report, “Your Majesties, disaster! Disaster! The monks have broken down the front gate!” The three demon kings said in great vexation, “These scoundrels are utterly insolent!” They immediately ordered their armor brought, arrayed themselves, each took up his weapon, and led the lesser demons out to meet the enemy. It was around the third watch, and the moon in midheaven shone as brightly as day. They came out and, without exchanging a word, immediately brandished their weapons. Wukong held off the battle-axe, Bajie engaged the broadsword, and Sha Wujing met the great cudgel. What a fine battle it was:

p.src: The three monks and three fiends fought for a long time, but neither side gained the upper hand. King Cold-Repelling gave a shout: “Underlings, come forward!” The demon horde rushed in together, each carrying a weapon. They quickly tripped Bajie to the ground, where several water-buffalo demons seized and dragged him into the cave to be bound. When Sha Wujing saw that Bajie was gone, the whole herd of ox demons raised a thunderous roar. He immediately drew back his precious staff, made a feint at King Dust-Repelling, and tried to flee. But the demons swarmed around him too. They dragged him off balance, and before he could struggle upright, he too was captured and bound. Wukong saw that the situation was hopeless, mounted his somersault cloud, and escaped. Bajie and Sha Wujing were then dragged before Tripitaka. Seeing them, Tripitaka’s eyes filled with tears. “Alas, you two have also fallen into their cruel hands. Where is Wukong?” Sha Wujing replied, “When Elder Brother saw us captured, he fled.” Tripitaka said, “Since he has escaped, he must have gone somewhere to seek help. But we do not know on what day we shall finally escape this net.” Master and disciples remained there in grief and misery, of which no more need be said.

p.src: Now Sun Wukong somersaulted back on his cloud to Ciyun Monastery. The monks came to meet him and asked, “Were you able to rescue Master Tang?” Wukong replied, “Hard to save him, hard indeed. Those fiends possess tremendous powers. The three of us fought the three of them for a long while, but they summoned their lesser demons, who first captured Bajie and then caught Sha Wujing. Only I was fortunate enough to escape.” The monks said fearfully, “Grandfather, if even one so skilled at riding clouds and mists as you cannot capture them, your master must surely have been murdered.” Wukong said, “Never fear, never fear. My master is secretly protected by the monastery guardians, the messengers, the gods of the cyclical signs, and other divinities. He has also eaten the herbal cinnabar elixir, so I doubt his life is in danger. It is only that these fiends are highly capable. Take good care of the horses and luggage while I go up to Heaven to seek reinforcements.” The monks asked timidly, “Grandfather, can you go up to Heaven too?” Wukong laughed. “The Celestial Palace was once my old home. In former days I was the Great Sage Equaling Heaven. Because I threw the Peach Banquet into disorder, the Buddha subdued me. Now, having no other recourse, I protect the Tang monk on his journey for the scriptures, redeeming my crimes through merit and supporting the righteous while destroying evil all along the road. My master was destined to suffer this ordeal, though none of you knew it.” Hearing this, the monks again knocked their heads upon the ground in reverence. Wukong went out through the gate, gave a whistle, and vanished at once.

p.src: The splendid Great Sage soon arrived outside the Western Gate of Heaven. There he suddenly saw the Great White Planet speaking with Virūḍhaka, Heavenly King of Growth, and the four great divine officers Yin, Zhu, Tao, and Xu. When they saw Wukong approaching, they hurriedly saluted him and asked, “Where are you going, Great Sage?” Wukong replied, “While escorting the Tang monk, we reached Mintian County in Jinping Prefecture, on the eastern frontier of India. The monks of the county’s Ciyun Monastery invited my master to stay and admire the Lantern Festival. When we came to Golden Lamp Bridge, there were three golden lamps whose fuel was fragrant butter oil worth more than fifty thousand taels of silver. Every year, it was said, Buddhas descended to bestow blessings and partake of it. As we watched, three figures of Buddhas did indeed descend. My master, unable to tell good from ill, stepped onto the bridge and bowed to them. I said they were no good, but they had already darkened the lamplight and swept away both the oil and my master in a gust of wind. I pursued the wind until dawn and reached a mountain, where fortunately the Four Duty Gods told me that it was called Green Dragon Mountain and contained the Xuanying Cave. Three fiends dwell in the cave, named Great King Cold-Dispeller, Great King Heat-Dispeller, and Great King Dust-Dispeller. I hurried to their gate to demand my master’s return and fought them for a time, but could not prevail. I then transformed myself and slipped inside. Seeing my master chained but unharmed, I freed him and tried to take him out, but they discovered us, and I had to flee. Later I returned with Bajie and Sha Wujing and fought bitterly, but they captured and bound those two as well. For this reason I have come especially to report to the Jade Emperor, learn their origins, and request heavenly generals to subdue them.” The Great White Planet gave a cold chuckle. “Since you fought those monsters face-to-face, Great Sage, could you not discern what they came from?” Wukong said, “I did, I did. They are a pack of bovine spirits. But their magic powers are formidable, and I cannot subdue them at once.” The Great White Planet said, “Those three are rhinoceros spirits. Because they bear the signs of celestial constellations, they cultivated enlightenment over many years and attained their true forms. They can also fly upon clouds and tread through mist. These creatures are exceedingly fond of cleanliness and constantly dislike the sight of their own shadows, so they are forever wishing to bathe in water. They have many varieties and names: si rhinoceroses, male rhinoceroses, bull rhinoceroses, spotted rhinoceroses, as well as humao, duoluo, and sky-communing flower-patterned rhinoceroses. All have three hairs in each pore and two horns, and when they travel through rivers and seas they can open passages through the water. As for Cold-Dispeller, Heat-Dispeller, and Dust-Dispeller, their horns all possess a noble potency; hence they took those names and styled themselves great kings. If you wish to capture them, they will submit as soon as they meet the four Wood-aligned bird constellations.” Wukong hurriedly bowed and asked, “Which are the four Wood-aligned bird constellations? Please, venerable Chang Geng, explain them to me one by one.” The Great White Planet smiled. “Those stars are stationed beyond the Palace of the Dipper and Ox and are arrayed throughout the firmament. Go and report to the Jade Emperor, and all will become clear.” Wukong clasped his hands in thanks and went straight through the Gate of Heaven.

p.src: Before long he reached the Hall of Perfect Light, where he first met the four great Celestial Masters Ge, Qiu, Zhang, and Xu. The Celestial Masters asked, “Where are you bound?” Wukong replied, “We recently reached the region of Jinping Prefecture. My master gave free rein to his contemplative nature and went to view the lanterns on the night of the festival, only to be carried off by demons. I could not subdue them, so I have come especially to report to the Jade Emperor and ask for aid.” The four Celestial Masters immediately escorted Wukong to the Hall of Miraculous Mist to present his memorial. When all had completed their courtesies, they related the entire affair. The Jade Emperor issued a decree: “Which contingent of heavenly troops should be assigned to assist him?” Wukong memorialized, “When I reached the Western Gate of Heaven just now, the Chang Geng Star told me that the monsters are rhinoceroses turned into spirits, and that only the four Wood-aligned bird constellations can subdue them.” The Jade Emperor at once ordered Celestial Master Xu to accompany Wukong to the Palace of the Dipper and Ox, summon the four Wood-aligned bird constellations, and send them down to the mortal world to subdue the monsters.

p.src: When they reached the outside of the palace, the stars of the Twenty-Eight Lunar Lodges were already there to receive them. The Celestial Master said, “By imperial decree, the four Wood-aligned bird constellations are to accompany the Great Sage Sun down to the mortal world and subdue demons.” At once the Wood Dragon of the Horn, Wood Xie of the Dipper, Wood Wolf of the Legs, and Wood An of the Well stepped out from the side and called in answer, “Great Sage Sun, where are we being summoned to subdue demons?” Wukong laughed. “So it was you four! That old Chang Geng kept it hidden from me, and I could not understand his meaning. Had he told me at once that he meant the four Wood Lodges among the Twenty-Eight, I would have come directly to invite you. Why trouble His Majesty for a decree?” The four Wood Lodges replied, “What are you saying, Great Sage? Without an imperial decree, which of us would dare leave his post without authorization? Where exactly is the place? Let us hurry there and back.” Wukong said, “It is in Xuanying Cave on Green Dragon Mountain, northeast of Jinping Prefecture. Rhinoceroses there have become spirits.” The Wood Xie of the Dipper, Wood Wolf of the Legs, and Wood Dragon of the Horn said, “If they truly are rhinoceroses turned into spirits, there is no need for all of us. The Well Lodge alone will suffice, for he can climb mountains to devour tigers and enter the sea to seize rhinoceroses.” Wukong said, “Those rhinoceroses are no ordinary moon-gazing beasts. They have attained the Way through cultivation, and each is a thousand years old. It would be best for all four of you to go; do not make excuses. If one of you should fail to capture them alone, would that not create still more trouble?” The Celestial Master said, “What are you talking about? The decree names all four of you. How can you refuse to go? Take flight without delay. I shall return to report compliance with the decree.” The Celestial Master then took his leave of Wukong and departed.

Let us hurry there and back.”

The Wood Xie of the Dipper, Wood Wolf of the Legs, and Wood Dragon of the Horn said, “If they truly are rhinoceroses turned into spirits, there is no need for all of us. The Well Lodge alone will suffice, for he can climb mountains to devour tigers and enter the sea to seize rhinoceroses.”

p.src: The Four Wood Mansions said, “Great Sage, do not hesitate. Go and challenge them first, and draw them out; we shall follow and strike.” Pilgrim stepped forward at once and cursed, “You oil-stealing fiends! Give me back my master!” The gate had been smashed down by Eight Rules, and several lesser fiends had propped a few planks across the opening. Hearing the abuse from within, they hurried in to report, “Your Majesties, the monk Sun is outside cursing us! ” Cold-Averting said, “He fled in defeat; why has he returned today? He must have found reinforcements somewhere.” Cold-Averting and Heat-Averting said, “Why fear any reinforcements of his? Bring our armor at once. All of you must surround him with care and not let him escape.” Knowing nothing of their impending doom, the fiends each seized spear or saber, waved banners, beat drums, and streamed from the cave. They shouted at Pilgrim, “You ape who never learns from a beating—you have come again!” Nothing angered Pilgrim more than the word “ape.” Gritting his teeth in fury, he raised his iron staff and struck. The three demon kings deployed their lesser fiends in a circular formation and trapped Pilgrim at its center. From the other side, each of the Four Wood Animal Stars brandished his weapon and cried, “Evil beasts! Stay your hands!” When the three demon kings saw the four stars, they were naturally terrified and all cried, “Disaster! Disaster! He has brought those destined to subdue us. Every one of you, flee for your lives!” Amid roars, bellows, gasps, and panting, all the lesser fiends revealed their true forms: they were mountain cattle, water buffalo, and yellow ox spirits, and they scattered wildly over the mountain. The three demon kings also resumed their true shapes. Dropping their hands and returning to four hooves, which struck like iron cannonballs, they fled straight toward the northeast. The Great Sage led Well Wood Wolf and Horn Wood Dragon in relentless pursuit, never slackening for an instant. Meanwhile, Dipper Wood Hyena and Straddling Legs Wood Wolf swept the eastern hollows, peaks, ravines, and valleys, killing or capturing every last ox spirit. They then went into Xuanying Cave and released Tripitaka, Eight Rules, and Sha Monk.

p.src: Sha Monk recognized the two stars, and joined the others in bowing his thanks. He asked, “How did you two come here to rescue us?” The two stars replied, “The Great Sage Sun petitioned the Jade Emperor, who issued a decree dispatching us to subdue the fiends and rescue you.” Tripitaka shed tears again and said, “Why has my disciple Wukong not come in?” The two stars said, “Those three old fiends are rhinoceroses. When they saw us, each sought only to save his own life and fled northeast, toward the Gen quarter. The Great Sage Sun has led Well Wood Wolf and Horn Wood Dragon in pursuit. We two swept away the herd of ox spirits and came here expressly to free the holy monk.” Tripitaka again bowed his head to the ground in thanks, then bowed toward Heaven. Eight Rules helped him up and said, “Master, excessive courtesy must conceal deceit; there is no need to keep bowing. The four stellar officers came first by the Jade Emperor’s sacred decree, and second through Elder Brother’s influence. Though the lesser fiends have now been swept away, we do not yet know whether the old fiends have been subdued. Let us gather the valuables, overturn this cave and destroy its roots, then return to the monastery and await Elder Brother.” Straddling Legs Wood Wolf said, “Marshal of the Heavenly Reeds speaks with reason. You and the Curtain-Raising General escort your master back to the monastery to rest, while we return toward the Gen quarter to meet the enemy.” Eight Rules said, “Exactly, exactly. You two should join them in the capture. You must wipe them out completely before you can properly report fulfillment of the decree.” The two stellar officers immediately set off in pursuit.

p.src: We shall say no more for now of how those three escaped death and returned to the monastery. Instead we tell how the two stellar officers, Dipper Wood Hyena and Straddling Legs Wood Wolf, rode their clouds straight northeast toward the Gen quarter in pursuit of the fiends, but could see no trace of them from the sky. Not until they reached the Western Ocean did they see from afar the Great Sage Sun shouting over the sea. They lowered their clouds and asked, “Great Sage, where have the fiends gone?” Pilgrim said angrily, “Why did you two not come to pursue and subdue them? And now you blunder in here asking foolish questions!” Dipper Wood Hyena said, “When I saw the Great Sage and the stars Well and Horn defeat the fiends and give chase, I supposed you would surely capture them. We two therefore swept away the lesser fiends and entered Xuanying Cave to rescue your master and junior disciples. We searched the mountain and burned the cave, then entrusted your master to your two junior brothers, who led him back to Ciyun Monastery in the prefectural city. When you had not returned after a long while, we came in pursuit and searched until we reached this place.” Only then was Pilgrim pleased. He thanked them, saying, “Then you have indeed rendered good service. Many thanks for your trouble. But I chased the three fiends here, and they dived beneath the sea. Well and Horn are pursuing them closely below, while they told old Sun to guard the shore. Since you two have arrived, guard the shore and cut off their escape while old Sun goes down once more.”

p.src: The fine Great Sage swung his staff, formed a spell with his fingers, opened a path through the water, and plunged straight into the depths. There he saw the three fiends beneath the sea, locked in a desperate struggle to the death with Well Wood Wolf and Horn Wood Dragon. He leaped forward and shouted, “Old Sun is here!” The fiends were holding off the two stellar officers but were hard-pressed and unable to free their hands. Suddenly hearing Pilgrim’s cry, they thought only of preserving the little life left to them, wheeled around, and fled toward the heart of the sea. The horns on these monsters’ heads were exceptionally skilled at dividing the waters; with a rushing roar, they forced open a clear path. Behind them, the two stellar officers and the Great Sage joined forces in pursuit.

p.src: Now in the Western Sea were a depth-sounding yaksha and an armored sea patrolman. From afar they saw rhinoceroses parting the waters and also recognized the Great Sage Equaling Heaven and the two celestial stars. They hurried to the Crystal Palace and reported breathlessly to the Dragon King, “Your Majesty, three rhinoceroses are being chased this way by the Great Sage Equaling Heaven and two celestial stars!” On hearing this, the old Dragon King Ao Shun summoned Crown Prince Mo’ang. “Muster the aquatic troops at once. Those rhinoceros spirits Cold-Averting, Heat-Averting, and Dust-Averting must have provoked Pilgrim Sun. Now that they have entered our sea, draw your blades quickly and assist him.” Ao Mo’ang received the order and hurriedly mustered the troops. In moments, turtles, soft-shelled turtles, giant turtles, alligators, and fish of every kind, together with shrimp soldiers and crab warriors, each grasped spear or saber. Shouting as one, they surged from the Crystal Palace and blocked the rhinoceros spirits’ path. Unable to advance, the rhinoceros spirits hastily retreated, only to find the stars Well and Horn and the Great Sage blocking them from behind. Panic broke their formation. Each fled for his own life, scattering in every direction, and Dust-Averting was soon surrounded by the old Dragon King and his troops. The Great Sage Sun was delighted at the sight and cried, “Steady, steady! Take him alive; I do not want him dead!” Mo’ang obeyed. They swarmed forward, overturned Dust-Averting, pierced his nose with an iron hook, bunched his hooves together, and bound him fast.

p.src: They all obeyed, took leave of the Dragon King and his son, and emerged from the Western Sea. p.src: At Ciyun Monastery, Bajie and Sha Monk had just escorted the Tang Monk through the gate when they heard Pilgrim speaking in midair. At once they left their master and set down the luggage, rode wind and cloud into the sky, and asked Pilgrim how the subjugation had gone. Pilgrim said, “One was bitten to death by Officer Well; we have sawn off its horns, flayed it, and brought them back. The other two have been captured alive and are here.” Bajie said, “Let us push these two down into the city so the officials and people can see them and know that we truly are holy beings and gods. May the four constellation lords kindly lower their clouds and descend with us to the prefectural hall, where we shall execute these monsters. The facts are proven and their crimes deserve it—what more is there to discuss?” The four constellation lords said, “Marshal of the Heavenly Reeds, you have lately become most reasonable and learned in the law. Excellent!” Bajie replied, “After being a monk all these years, I have picked up a little.” The gods duly pushed the rhinoceros demons down and descended in a cluster of many-colored clouds above the prefectural hall. The prefectural and county officials and everyone within and beyond the city were so awed that every family set out an incense altar and every household worshiped the celestial gods.

p.src: Before long, the monks of Ciyun Monastery carried the elder in a sedan chair through the prefectural gate. Meeting Pilgrim, he repeatedly expressed his thanks: “We are indebted to the exalted constellation lords for rescuing us. I was constantly anxious because I could not see my worthy disciples, but happily you have now returned victorious. Yet in what direction did you pursue these monsters before capturing them?” Pilgrim replied, “After leaving you the day before yesterday, old Sun went up to Heaven to investigate. Venus, the Great White Planet, recognized the fiends as rhinoceroses and directed me to summon the four Wood-associated animal constellations. I reported the matter to the Jade Emperor, who graciously issued a decree commissioning them. We went straight to the cave mouth and fought, but the demon kings fled. Then the Dipper and Stride constellation lords kindly rescued you, Master. Old Sun joined forces with the Well and Horn constellation lords and pursued the demons all the way to the great Western Ocean. There, thanks also to the Dragon King, who sent his son with troops to assist us, we captured them and brought them here for judgment.” The elder praised them and thanked them without end. He also saw the chief prefectural and county officials and their assistants burning tall precious candles and whole measures of incense as they bowed in worship toward those above.

p.src: The prefectural and county officials detained the master and his three disciples, laid out a grand vegetarian feast, and invited local dignitaries from everywhere to attend upon them. Meanwhile they issued a proclamation informing soldiers and civilians that from the following year golden lamps were not to be set out, and that the compulsory service imposed on the wealthy households to purchase oil was abolished forever. At the same time they ordered butchers to slaughter and flay the rhinoceroses, tan and smoke-dry their hides, and make them into armor; the meat was distributed among the officials and others. They also drew upon unallocated funds from fines to buy vacant land from the people and build a temple to the four constellation lords who had descended to subdue the demons. They erected living shrines for the Tang Monk and his three disciples as well, setting up steles and carving inscriptions at each, so that the story might be handed down through the ages in gratitude.

u.src: The prefectural and county officials detained the master and his three disciples, laid out a grand vegetarian feast, and invited local dignitaries from everywhere to attend upon them.

Meanwhile they issued a proclamation informing soldiers and civilians that from the following year golden lamps were not to be set out, and that the compulsory service imposed on the wealthy households to purchase oil was abolished forever.
At the same time they ordered butchers to slaughter and flay the rhinoceroses, tan and smoke-dry their hides, and make them into armor;
the meat was distributed among the officials and others.

ja: とうそうしていよんにん
u.src: They also drew upon unallocated funds from fines to buy vacant land from the people and build a temple to the four constellation lords who had descended to subdue the demons. They erected living shrines for the Tang Monk and his three disciples as well, setting up steles and carving inscriptions at each, so that the story might be handed down through the ages in gratitude.

p.src: The master and disciples therefore put their minds at ease and accepted the hospitality. Moreover, the two hundred and forty wealthy households responsible for the lamp oil took turns rewarding and inviting them, without wasting a single moment. Bajie enjoyed himself to his heart’s content. From each kind of treasure recovered from the cave, he tucked a little into his sleeve as a reward for every family’s vegetarian banquet. After staying a full month, they were still unable to set out. The elder instructed them, “Wukong, give all the remaining treasure to the monks of Ciyun Monastery as our return gift. Without telling those wealthy households, let us leave before daybreak. I fear that if we remain engrossed in pleasure, we shall delay our scripture quest, incur the Buddha’s displeasure, and bring fresh calamity upon ourselves. That would be most unfortunate.” Pilgrim accordingly made every arrangement just described.

p.src: At the fifth watch the next morning, they rose early and called Bajie to prepare the horse. The fool, well fed with carefree drinking and dining, had been sleeping deeply. Starting awake, he said, “Why prepare the horse so early?” Pilgrim shouted, “Master says we are leaving!” The fool rubbed his face. “Our elder is being unreasonable again. All two hundred and forty wealthy households mean to invite us, and we have eaten only thirty-odd filling vegetarian meals. Why is he making old Hog go hungry again?” Hearing this, the elder cursed him: “You gluttonous oaf! Stop talking nonsense and get up at once. If you argue again, I shall have Wukong knock out your teeth with his gold-banded cudgel.” At the mention of a beating, the fool panicked. “Master has changed this time! Usually you dote on me, protect me because I am clumsy, and intercede whenever Brother means to beat me; why are you so fierce today that you are actually telling him to beat me?” Pilgrim said, “Master is angry because your appetite is delaying our journey. Hurry and pack the luggage and prepare the horse if you want to escape a beating!” The fool truly feared a beating. He sprang up, dressed, and shouted to Sha Monk, “Get up quickly—the beating is coming!” Sha Monk also leaped up, and they each finished packing. The elder waved his hand. “Quietly, quietly! Do not wake the monks.” They hurriedly mounted, opened the monastery gate, found the road, and departed. Of this departure it is rightly said:
